blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to recover well-exposed and perceptually faithful images from severely degraded observations. Recent diffusion-based generative methods achieve strong perceptual quality by leveraging powerful image priors, but their iterative sampling incurs substantial computational cost, limiting practical deployment. Despite recent efficiency gains in generative LLIE, high-quality enhancement with a single function evaluation and low overall computation remains challenging, particularly under diverse real-world low-light conditions. We introduce GLOW-FM, a one-step latent flow-matching framework for efficient generative LLIE. GLOW-FM performs conditional transport in the latent space of a frozen Tiny-VAE and leverages Terminal Velocity Matching (TVM) to enable enhancement with a single function evaluation. Matched comparisons with alternative one-step objectives support TVM as an effective design choice, and, to the best of our knowledge, this is its first adaptation to image restoration and specifically to LLIE. Extensive experiments on challenging real-world benchmarks demonstrate that GLOW-FM achieves competitive image quality and state-of-the-art cross-dataset generalization while requiring only a single function evaluation and 34 GFLOPs for the small variant. These findings highlight the potential of GLOW-FM to bring generative LLIE closer to practical deployment through single-step inference and compact latent modeling. Code will be made publicly available upon publication.

blocks.en: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to recover well-exposed and visually pleasing images from observations captured under insufficient illumination. Real-world low-light images often exhibit a complex combination of degradations, including severe underexposure, sensor noise, color distortion, reduced contrast, detail loss, and local saturation, which vary significantly across cameras and imaging conditions, making LLIE a challenging problem in real-world imaging [ 8 , 6 , 28 ] . Beyond degrading visual quality, these artifacts also impair downstream computer vision tasks such as object detection and recognition, whose performance declines substantially on poorly exposed inputs [ 32 ] . Consequently, LLIE seeks not only to enhance image appearance but also to restore perceptually faithful content that supports reliable high-level vision applications [ 16 , 40 ] .
blocks.zh: 低光图像增强(LLIE)旨在从光照不足所摄取的观测结果中取回暴露良好的视觉取悦的图像. 真实世界的低光影像往往表现出复杂的退化组合,包括严重接触不足,感官噪音,颜色扭曲,对比度降低,细节损失,以及局部饱和等,相机和成像条件差异很大,使得LIE在真实世界成像[8,6,28]中成为一个具有挑战性的问题. 除了降低视觉质量外,这些文物还损害下游计算机视觉任务,如物体探测和识别,其性能在曝光度低的投入上大幅下降[32]. 因此,LLIE不仅寻求增强图像外观,还寻求恢复支持可靠高水平视觉应用的感知忠实内容[16,40].

blocks.en:
Regression-based LLIE methods provide strong distortion performance and efficient inference [ 4 , 5 , 62 , 68 , 61 , 69 , 58 , 7 , 59 , 45 , 54 ] . These approaches typically optimize distortion-oriented objectives and are effective at recovering visibility and suppressing noise, but often struggle under severe degradation, where substantial information loss makes enhancement inherently ambiguous. Trained with pixel-wise objectives, they tend to produce overly smooth results and suppress fine details [ 3 ] .
To address this limitation, generative models [ 19 , 65 , 21 , 55 , 66 , 22 , 17 ] have emerged as a powerful LLIE paradigm, learning the distribution of natural images and leveraging strong image priors to recover realistic textures and structures that are difficult to reconstruct with deterministic networks. These methods demonstrate substantial improvements in perceptual quality and robustness under severe degradations.
However, these gains come at the cost of iterative sampling, resulting in high computational complexity and limiting practical deployment, particularly for high-resolution enhancement in resource-constrained applications such as smartphone camera image processing.
blocks.zh:
基于倒退的LLIE方法提供了强大的扭曲性能和高效率的推论[4,5,62,68,61,69,58,7,59,45,54]. 这些办法通常优化了以扭曲为导向的目标,有效地恢复能见度和抑制噪音,但往往在严重的退化下挣扎,因为大量信息损失使增强本身变得模糊不清。 以像素为目的的训练,往往产生过于平滑的结果并压制精细的细节[3].
为解决这一局限,基因模型[19,65,21,55,66,22,17]已作为一个强大的LIE范式出现,学习自然图像的分布,并利用强图像前身来恢复现实的纹理和结构,这些纹理和结构难以用定型网络重建. 这些方法表明,在严重退化的情况下,认知质量和稳健性大有改善。
然而,这些收益是以迭代取样为代价的,导致计算复杂性高并限制了实际部署,特别是在智能手机相机图像处理等受资源限制的应用程序的高分辨率增强方面。

blocks.en:
To address this limitation, several efficient generative LLIE frameworks have recently been proposed [ 20 , 70 , 25 ] . These methods significantly reduce the required number of function evaluations (NFEs) compared to conventional diffusion models. Nevertheless, they still rely on iterative refinement procedures and diffusion-inspired architectures whose computational complexity remains substantial. For example, WCDM [ 20 ] requires 10 NFEs and approximately 90 GFLOPs during inference, while ReDDiT [ 25 ] reduces sampling to 2 NFEs but still requires roughly 128 GFLOPs.
Consequently, while recent generative LLIE approaches have substantially reduced sampling cost, achieving high-quality enhancement with a single inference step and a low overall computational budget remains an active challenge, particularly across diverse and demanding real-world low-light conditions.

为解决这一局限性,最近提出了几个高效的基因有限责任公司框架[20、70、25]。 这些方法与传统的传播模式相比,大大减少了所需的功能评价数量. 然而,它们仍然依赖反复不断的完善程序和传播启发的架构,其计算复杂性仍然很大。 例如,WCDM[20]在推论中需要10个NFE和约90个GFLOP,而ReDDIT[25]将采样量减少到2个NFE,但仍需要约128个GFLOP.

blocks.en:
In this work, we address this challenge by introducing an efficient G enerative Low -Light image enhancement with one-step latent F low M atching ( GLOW-FM ).
Our approach leverages Terminal Velocity Matching (TVM) [ 71 ] , which enables direct prediction of the normal-light image, eliminating the need for iterative sampling during inference.
Comparisons with standard Flow Matching [ 30 , 31 ] , Consistency Flow Matching [ 63 ] , and MeanFlow [ 12 ] establish Terminal Velocity Matching (TVM) [ 71 ] as a deliberate design choice for single-step LLIE. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first adaptation of TVM to image restoration, and specifically to LLIE.
GLOW-FM learns a conditional transport that maps degraded low-light representations directly to their well-exposed counterparts in the latent space of a frozen Tiny-VAE [ 49 ] . Operating in this compact latent space substantially reduces computational cost while preserving the expressive power of generative modeling. Moreover, latent representations capture semantic image structure while suppressing dataset-specific variations, improving restoration and generalization [ 51 , 29 , 48 ] .

Extensive experiments on challenging real-world low-light benchmarks [ 45 , 54 ] demonstrate that GLOW-FM provides an effective generative prior for low-light enhancement while operating under small inference budgets. Despite requiring only a single NFE, our method achieves image quality competitive with recent efficient generative LLIE approaches and consistently exhibits strong cross-dataset generalization as shown in Fig. 1 .
These results suggest that latent flow matching, combined with one-step TVM estimation, offers a promising direction toward practical, high-quality, and computationally efficient low-light image enhancement.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We introduce GLOW-FM, an efficient generative framework for low-light image enhancement (LLIE) based on latent flow matching. By performing enhancement in a compact latent space with a lightweight Tiny-VAE and a one-step flow formulation, GLOW-FM achieves high restoration quality at low computational cost. • We establish Terminal Velocity Matching (TVM) as the strongest overall one-step objective for LLIE through matched comparisons with Rectified Flow, Consistency Flow Matching, and MeanFlow. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first adaptation of TVM to image restoration, specifically LLIE. • We achieve state-of-the-art cross-dataset generalization compared to generative and non-generative baselines, while maintaining competitive image quality and improved efficiency over existing generative LLIE methods.

blocks.en: 2.1 Generative Low-Light Image Enhancement
blocks.zh: 2.1 基因低光图像增强

blocks.en:
A large body of LLIE research focuses on directly regressing a normal-light image from a low-light input using Retinex decomposition [ 26 ] , illumination estimation, and deep neural networks [ 5 , 62 , 45 , 4 ] . While these approaches are computationally efficient, they often produce overly smooth results and struggle to capture the diversity of plausible normal-light reconstructions.
The recent success of diffusion models [ 18 ] in image generation has motivated their adoption for high-quality low-light image enhancement [ 65 , 19 , 25 , 70 , 20 , 17 , 21 ] .
Diff-Retinex [ 65 ] formulates enhancement as Retinex decomposition followed by conditional diffusion-based reconstruction of reflectance and illumination components. GSAD [ 19 ] introduces a global structure-aware diffusion framework that combines curvature-based regularization with uncertainty-guided optimization to preserve scene structure and focus restoration on challenging regions. Subsequent work has largely aimed to reduce the high computational cost of diffusion sampling. ReDDiT [ 25 ] uses trajectory matching distillation in a reflectance-aware residual space to reduce the NFEs required at inference. PyDiff [ 70 ] performs denoising in a coarse-to-fine resolution pyramid and employs a global correction module to mitigate brightness and color inconsistencies. WCDM [ 20 ] accelerates inference by conducting diffusion in the wavelet domain on low-frequency sub-bands while restoring high-frequency details through a dedicated branch.

to guide a transformer-based restoration network, while
LightenDiffusion [ 21 ] combines latent Retinex
decomposition with diffusion for unsupervised LLIE. Related concurrent
preprints, IllumFlow [ 57 ] and
Consist-Retinex [ 60 ] , further explore one-step
generative LLIE through Retinex-based decomposition.

blocks.en: 2.2 Generative Model Acceleration
blocks.zh: 2.2 基因模型加速

blocks.en:
Generative diffusion and flow models have achieved remarkable success
across a wide range of image-generation tasks. Their strong priors have
also motivated applications to image restoration, where the goal is to
recover a clean image from a degraded observation. InDI [ 11 ] performs restoration through direct iteration, while
IR-SDE [ 35 ] models the restoration trajectory using a
mean-reverting stochastic process. Bridge-matching
methods [ 46 ] further formalize transport between degraded and
clean endpoint distributions, and flow-based approaches such as
FlowIE [ 73 ] and PnP-Flow [ 37 ] extend this formulation
to image restoration.
Despite their strong restoration capabilities, these methods commonly
require iterative sampling, resulting in substantial inference cost.
Early acceleration approaches employed fast post-hoc
samplers [ 47 , 34 , 23 ] , reducing inference from hundreds of
steps to tens, often at the expense of quality under aggressive
acceleration.
More recently, flow-based objectives have been developed specifically
for efficient one- and few-step generation. Rectified
Flow [ 31 ] learns straighter transport trajectories,
while Consistency Flow Matching [ 63 ] regularizes the velocity
field for few-step inference. ELIR [ 9 ] applies Consistency Flow
Matching to image restoration in the latent space of a Tiny
AutoEncoder. MeanFlow [ 12 ] learns mean transport trajectories,
whereas TVM [ 71 ] learns finite displacements between arbitrary
timesteps for high-fidelity one- and few-step generation.
Despite these advances, efficient flow-based generation remains
relatively unexplored for LLIE. Building upon TVM, we introduce a
single-step latent flow-matching framework for efficient low-light
enhancement.

Beyond its reported strong one-step performance, we motivate TVM for restoration through theoretical analysis. Under the TVM regularity conditions [ 71 , Theorem 1] and a Lipschitz assumption on the decoder, we derive a bound on the pixel-space Wasserstein-2 distance [ 41 ] between the restored-image and target normal-light distributions in terms of the TVM objectives and autoencoder reconstruction error. This links TVM training to pixel-space restoration; the complete theorem and proof are provided in Appendix B . We next describe TVM’s adaptation to our restoration setting, training and inference, and the design choices enabling efficient generation.

blocks.en: 3.4 Efficient Latent Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.4 高效的地下建筑

blocks.en: Compact Latent Representation. Operating in latent space is central to the efficiency of GLOW-FM. Instead of applying the flow model to full-resolution RGB images, the VAE encoder maps the input into a lower-dimensional representation with reduced spatial resolution. The learned transport therefore acts on a compact latent grid, lowering the cost of each function evaluation and making low-NFE inference more practical.
blocks.zh: 近卫代表 在潜在空间运作对GLOW-FM的效率至关重要。 VAE编码器没有将流出模型应用于全分辨率的RGB图像,而是将输入图映射为空间分辨率降低的下维代表. 因此,所学得的运输在紧凑的潜在网格上发挥作用,降低了每项职能评价的成本,并使低额NFE推论更切合实际。

blocks.en:
The latent space also provides a useful restoration prior. Since the VAE is pretrained on a broad natural-image distribution, its representation captures reusable image structure while suppressing some pixel-level noise and dataset-specific degradation patterns. Prior work has similarly shown that pretrained latent representations can support robust image restoration and domain generalization [ 51 , 29 , 48 ] . As a result, the flow model learns exposure and appearance corrections in a natural-image latent domain rather than relying solely on dataset-specific pixel statistics.
For the autoencoder, inspired by [ 9 ] , we use Tiny AutoEncoder for Stable Diffusion (TAESD) [ 49 ] , a lightweight distilled alternative to the Stable Diffusion VAE (SD-VAE) [ 44 ] . TAESD preserves an SD-VAE-compatible latent interface while substantially reducing the cost of encoding and decoding. In our implementation, replacing SD-VAE with TAESD reduces encoding/decoding GFLOPs by 15 × 15\times and parameter count by 33 × 33\times , with minimal loss in end-to-end restoration performance. This is important for low-NFE generation, where the flow model requires only one or a few evaluations and the VAE cost becomes a significant part of the total inference budget.
blocks.zh:
潜在的空间还提供了有用的前期恢复。 由于VAE在广义的自然映像分布上被预先训练出,它的表现可以捕捉到可再使用的映像结构,同时抑制出一些像素级噪声和数据集特有的退化模式. 先前的工作同样表明,经过预先训练的潜在表现可以支持稳健的图像恢复和域通化[51、29、48]。 因此,流出模型学习了自然成像潜入域中的曝光和外观修正,而不仅仅依赖于数据集特定像素统计.
对于受[9]所启发的自定义编码器,我们使用"TAESD"(TAESD)[49]的"Tiny Auto Encoder",是一种轻量级的蒸馏替代"SD-VAE"(SD-VAE)[44]. TAESD保留了SD-VAE相容的潜在接口,同时大幅降低了编码和解码的成本. 在我们的实施中,用TAESD取代了SD-VAE,将编码/解码GFLOP减少15×15分,参数数减少33×33分,末端恢复性能损失最小. 这对于低水平的NFE生成很重要,其中流量模型只需要一个或几个评价,而VAE成本成为推论总预算的重要一环.

blocks.en: HDiT two-time flow model. We implement the two-time conditioned flow model F θ ​ ( z t , t , s ) F_{\theta}(z_{t},t,s) with an Hourglass Diffusion Transformer (HDiT) backbone. HDiT combines the multi-scale efficiency of U-Net-like architectures with the representation capacity of diffusion transformers [ 10 ] . Unlike standard DiT-style architectures [ 42 ] , which apply global attention at every resolution and incur O ⁡ ( n 2 ) O(n^{2}) attention cost, HDiT restricts global attention to low-resolution stages and uses fixed-window neighborhood attention at higher resolutions, yielding linear O ⁡ ( n ) O(n) scaling with the number of latent image tokens. This design is useful for GLOW-FM because latent restoration requires both global exposure/color correction and preservation of spatially aligned local content from the degraded input, while keeping the two-time flow model efficient at inference.
blocks.zh: HDIT双回流模式. 我们用一个小时玻璃分解变压器(HDIT)主干线,实施双时有条件的F θ (z t, t, s) (z_{t} (z_{t}),t, s. HDIT结合了U-Net类架构的多尺度效率与扩散变压器的能见度[10]. 与标准DiT风格的架构[42]不同,该架构将全球注意力应用到每个分辨率上,并发生O ⁡ (n 2) O (n^{ (n^{2}) 注意成本,HDiT将全球注意力限制在低分辨率相间,并在高分辨率时使用固定窗口相邻的注意力,产生线性O ⁡ (n) O (n) 与潜在图像符号的数量相适应. 这种设计对GLOW-FM很有用,因为潜在还原既需要全球曝光/颜色校正,也需要从已退化的输入中保留空间一致的局部内容,同时保持双相流模型在推论上的效率.

blocks.en: Datasets. We evaluate GLOW-FM on both paired and unpaired real-world LLIE benchmarks. Our primary benchmark is LSD-DLL [ 45 ] , a large-scale dataset designed to improve the realism and diversity of LLIE evaluation. Unlike many earlier low-light datasets [ 7 , 64 , 15 ] , which are limited by synthetic darkening, controlled capture settings, or restricted sensor coverage, LSD-DLL [ 45 ] provides real low and normal-light image pairs captured across diverse scenes and devices in the wild using dynamic exposure calibration and multi-frame alignment to obtain more realistic paired data. As a result, it better captures phenomena such as sensor noise, spatially varying illumination, and color distortions that are often underrepresented in existing LLIE benchmarks. These properties motivated its use as the benchmark dataset in [ 8 ] . LSD-DLL also provides the LSD-U test split, which consists of unpaired low-light images captured with unseen devices and enables evaluation of generalization beyond the paired training distribution. To complement LSD-DLL, we additionally evaluate on UHD-LOL4K [ 54 ] , a high-resolution LLIE benchmark, and LOL-v1 [ 7 ] , one of the most widely used datasets in the LLIE literature.
blocks.zh: 数据集. 我们评价GLOW-FM的成对和未成熟的现实世界LIE基准。 我们的主要基准是LSD-DLL[45],这是一个大规模数据集,旨在改进LLIE评价的现实性和多样性. 与早期许多低光数据集[7,64,15]不同的是,LSD-DLL在合成变暗,可控捕捉设置,或受限的传感器覆盖下受到限制,LSD-DLL[45]通过动态曝光校正和多帧对接,提供在野外不同场景和装置上捕获到的真实低光和常光的图像对等,以获得更现实的配对数据. 因此,它能更好地捕捉感应噪声,空间相变发光等现象,并捕捉在现有的LIE基准中往往代表性不足的色彩扭曲. 这些属性促使它被用作[8]中的基准数据集. LSD-DLL还提供LSD-U测试分解,由用隐形设备捕获的未发光低光图像所组成,并且能够评价组合训练分布之外的一般化. 为了补充LSD-DLL,我们额外评价UHD-LOL4K [54],一个高分辨率的LIE基准,以及LOL-v1 [7],LIE文献中最广泛使用的数据集之一.

blocks.en: Following [ 25 , 19 , 20 ] , we further evaluate cross-dataset generalization by training on LOL-v2-Syn [ 64 ] and testing directly on five widely used unpaired real-world low-light datasets: DICM [ 27 ] , LIME [ 14 ] , MEF [ 36 ] , NPE [ 53 ] , and VV [ 50 ] . Since these datasets do not provide paired reference images, they are evaluated using no-reference image quality metrics.
blocks.zh: 继[25,19,20]后,我们通过LOL-v2-Syn[64]的培训,并直接测试被广泛使用的5个被广泛使用的真实世界低光数据集,进一步评价了跨数据集通论:DICM [27],LIME [14],MEF [36],NPE [53],和VV [50]. 由于这些数据集不提供配对的参考图像,因此使用无参考图像质量衡量标准对其进行评价.

blocks.en:
Evaluation metrics. For paired benchmarks, we evaluate both distortion and perceptual quality.
Distortion is measured using PSNR and SSIM [ 56 ] , while perceptual similarity is assessed using LPIPS [ 67 ] . We additionally evaluate perceptual image quality using the no-reference metrics NIQE [ 39 ] and MUSIQ [ 24 ] . For unpaired benchmarks, where ground-truth reference images are unavailable, we follow [ 20 ] and report the no-reference perceptual quality metrics NIQE [ 39 ] and BRISQUE [ 38 ] . Results are averaged over five evaluation seeds; full mean and STD results are provided in Appendix F .

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
Low-light image enhancement remains challenging because noise, color shifts, and information loss make faithful restoration ambiguous.
Although recent generative LLIE methods have reduced sampling cost, combining single-step inference, low overall computation, and robust performance across real-world conditions remains challenging.

blocks.en: In this work, we address this challenge with GLOW-FM, an efficient generative LLIE framework based on one-step latent flow matching. By combining efficiency-aware latent flow matching with Terminal Velocity Matching, GLOW-FM enables single-NFE enhancement while preserving generative priors for realistic restoration. Experiments show competitive quality, improved efficiency, and state-of-the-art cross-dataset generalization, suggesting a practical direction for robust and efficient generative low-light enhancement.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们通过GLOW-FM来应对这一挑战,GLOW-FM是一个基于一步一步潜在流量匹配的高效基因型LIE框架. GLOW-FM将认识到效率的潜在流量与终端高速匹配结合起来,使单NFE增强,同时为现实的恢复保留基因前科。 实验显示竞争质量,提高效率,以及最先进的跨数据集通论,为强而高效的基因低光增强提出了实际方向.

blocks.en: Unless otherwise specified, all experiments use a frozen Tiny-VAE encoder/decoder while optimizing only the latent flow model. Models are trained on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs with a per-GPU batch size of 2 (effective batch size 16) for approximately 100k optimization steps. Optimization uses AdamW with a learning rate of 10 − 5 10^{-5} , betas ( 0.9 , 0.95 ) (0.9,0.95) , weight decay 0.01 0.01 , gradient clipping at norm 1.0 1.0 , and EMA decay 0.9999 0.9999 . The learning rate follows a 5k-step warmup with cosine decay to a minimum learning-rate ratio of 0.01 0.01 . Training uses random 2048 × 2048 2048\times 2048 crops for LSD-DLL and UHD-LOL4K, and 384 × 384 384\times 384 crops for LOL-v1. Validation uses a batch size of 1 and is performed at the original image resolution. Source latents are perturbed with Gaussian noise using σ = 0.01 \sigma=0.01 during training and σ = 0 \sigma=0 during evaluation. Unless otherwise specified, all reported results use a single NFE.
blocks.zh: 除非另有说明,所有实验都使用被冻结的Tiny-VAE编码器/解码器,而只优化了潜流模型. 模型在8个NVIDIA H100 GPU上进行训练,每GPU批量尺寸为2个(有效批量尺寸为16个),用于约100k优化步骤. 优化使用 AdamW,学习率为10−5 10^{-5},β (0.9,0.95) (0.9,0.95),重量衰减 0.01 0.01, 在规范 1.0 上进行梯度剪接, EMA衰减 0.9999 0.9999 . 学习率跟随了5k步的热身,并伴有余弦衰变,最低学习率为0.010.01. 培训随机使用2048×2048 2048\时为LSD-DLL和UHD-LOL4K的2048个作物,而LOL-v1的384×384\时为384个作物. 验证使用批量尺寸为1并按原始图像分辨率进行. 源潜在物被高斯语噪声所扰动,在训练时使用相差0.01\sigma=0.01;在评价时使用相差0\sigma=0. 除非另有说明,所有报告的结果都使用单一的非常规外线。

blocks.en: We use the official madebyollin/taesd3 [ 49 ] checkpoint as a frozen Tiny-VAE image tokenizer. TAESD is a lightweight autoencoder distilled from the Stable Diffusion VAE (SD-VAE) [ 44 ] , providing a compact alternative for encoding and decoding images. RGB images are encoded into 16-channel latent representations, and the flow model operates entirely in this latent space. The encoder and decoder remain frozen throughout training, and no additional latent normalization is applied. During inference, the predicted latent representation is decoded using the same frozen Tiny-VAE decoder before computing image-space evaluation metrics.
blocks.zh: 我们使用makebyollin/taesd3[49]检查站作为冷冻的Tiny-VAE图像显示器. TAESD是从稳定分化VAE(SD-VAE)[44]中分出的一种轻量级自编码器,为编码和解码图像提供了紧凑的替代品. RGB图像被编码成16个通道的潜在表达,流模型完全在这个潜在空间中运行. 编码器和解码器在整个培训期间一直被冻结,没有实行额外的潜在正常化。 在推论期间,在计算出图像空间评价指标之前,使用同一种被冻结的Tiny-VAE解码器来解码预测的潜在表示.

blocks.en: For LSD-DLL and UHD-LOL4K, we independently retrained every baseline on the corresponding training set using the authors’ official code and method-specific training recipe. We retained the official architecture, optimization settings, and training schedule, modifying only the dataset configuration as necessary. For LOL-v1, we used the official pretrained weights released by the respective authors whenever available. TFFormer was the only exception: because no official LOL-v1 checkpoint was available, we also trained it from scratch on the LOL-v1 training set. Unless otherwise stated, the training details below describe our retraining on LSD-DLL and UHD-LOL4K, and all models were trained using NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
blocks.zh: 对于LSD-DLL和UHD-LOL4K,我们使用作者的官方代码和特定方法的训练方法,独立地重新训练了对应训练集的每一个基线. 我们保留了官方架构,优化设置,以及培训时间表,只根据需要修改数据集配置. 对于LOL-v1,我们使用了各作者在有时间时发布的官方预训重量. TFFFormer是唯一的例外:因为没有官方的LOL-v1检查站,我们也从头开始在LOL-v1训练集上训练. 除非另有说明,下文的培训细节描述了我们在LSD-DLL和UHD-LOL4K上的再培训,所有模型都使用NVIDIA H100 GPU进行训练.

blocks.en: We trained a separate TFFormer model from scratch on each of LSD-DLL, UHD-LOL4K, and LOL-v1. TFFormer was optimized using an Adam optimizer with hyperparameters β 1 = 0.9 \beta_{1}=0.9 and β 2 = 0.99 \beta_{2}=0.99 . We set the initial learning rate to 10 − 4 10^{-4} and adjusted it after 100,000 steps using PyTorch’s ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler [ 43 ] . We trained each model for 300,000 steps on a single GPU using a batch size of 24 and 128 × 128 128\times 128 RGB patches. Additionally, we used a low-light regularization coefficient of λ R = 0.2 \lambda_{R}=0.2 for the combined reconstruction and luminance–chrominance objective.

blocks.en: Without TVM warmup, the TVM objective is introduced before the flow-matching model has learned a meaningful low-to-normal-light transport. As a result, the displacement objective is optimized with respect to an immature velocity field, leading the optimization toward an inferior solution. In contrast, the proposed warmup schedule allows the flow-matching objective to first establish a reliable transport before introducing the TVM objective, resulting in improved PSNR and substantially better NIQE at convergence.

blocks.en: This section presents additional qualitative comparisons across several benchmarks, including unseen-device generalization on LSD-U ( Fig. 10 ), high-resolution enhancement on UHD-LOL4K ( Fig. 11 ) and LSD-DLL ( Fig. 13 , Fig. 14 ), and low-resolution enhancement on LOL-v1 ( Fig. 12 ).
